summary:
Space Never Forgets is an interactive digital museum called Space Relics Explorer, built to show students what happens to NASA’s robotic explorers after their missions end—and why their discoveries stay with us forever.

Instead of reading a textbook, students step into the shoes of planetary detectives. Through interactive timelines, hands-on Explorer Quests, and direct links to real NASA data—including NASA Mars Trek, the NASA Planetary Data System (PDS), and JPL’s Voyager Interstellar Mission—visitors uncover the real science behind three iconic spacecraft: Surveyor 3 on the Moon, Opportunity on Mars, and Voyager 1 in interstellar space.

We created this project because space exploration isn't just about launching rockets; it's about the curiosity and knowledge those machines pass down to us. Even when a rover falls silent on Mars or a lander rests on the Moon, its data lives on to inspire the next generation of explorers.
details:
What It Does & How It Works

Space Never Forgets (featuring the Space Relics Explorer digital museum) is an interactive web platform and 7-slide documentary presentation designed to turn space history into an active, hands-on investigation for students. Instead of presenting passive walls of text, the platform organizes humanity's robotic exploration across three distinct fates: missions that completed their work (Surveyor 3 on the Moon), explorers that fell silent after extraordinary journeys (Opportunity on Mars), and pioneers still calling home from deep space (Voyager 1).

Visitors navigate through four interactive museum modules:

1. Mission Timelines: Interactive launch-to-legacy tracks highlighting key engineering and scientific milestones for each spacecraft.

2. 3D Relic Maps: Direct integration with NASA Mars Trek so students can explore Martian elevation, terrain, and Opportunity's landing region.

3. Science Logs: Curated breakdowns connecting spacecraft observations—such as Martian hematite "blueberries," neutral-pH clay minerals, lunar soil mechanics, and interstellar plasma—directly to raw records in the NASA Planetary Data System (PDS).

4. Explorer Quests: An interactive mini-challenge where students act as planetary detectives, analyzing real mission clues to uncover what each discovery proved.

Benefits & Intended Impact

Traditional space education often focuses on rocket launches while overlooking what happens to spacecraft years later—and how their archived data continues to drive science. Our goal is to make middle and high school students feel like real explorers rather than passive listeners. By lowering the barrier to official NASA datasets and pairing hard science with emotional storytelling, Space Relics Explorer inspires young learners to see that even after hardware powers down, its knowledge stays with humanity forever.

Tools & Software Used

- Web Development & UI Design: Built using Canva Websites and Canva Code for responsive layout, interactive mission timeline switching, and live quiz scoring.

- Presentation & Visual Storytelling: Designed in Google Slides using a 7-slide documentary narrative structure.

- Scientific Data & Research: Powered by open planetary science archives from NASA Mars Trek, the NASA Planetary Data System (PDS), and JPL’s Voyager Interstellar Mission status logs.

Creativity & Key Design Considerations

Our main creative decision was treating the project like a cinematic museum exhibition rather than a school report. When designing the experience, we prioritized three core factors:

- Scientific Accuracy vs. Accessibility: We kept the tone engaging and easy for students to scan while ensuring every discovery—from Apollo 12's camera retrieval on Surveyor 3 to Voyager 1's heliosphere crossing—was grounded in real NASA mission records.

- Visual Clarity & Transparency: We used a dark-space telemetry aesthetic to keep focus on the missions and clearly distinguished between curated educational summaries, illustrative visuals, and live NASA data portals.

- Actionable Exploration: Rather than keeping students trapped on one page, every module serves as a launchpad into official NASA tools so curious learners can continue investigating real planetary data on their own.
